newsitem.title: MALTA: Ministers at Malta talks look to boost human rights.
newsitem.headline: Ministers at Malta talks look to boost human rights.

text.p: Ministers from the European Union and 12 Mediterranean countries were to consider on Tuesday ways to improve human rights in the region, combat "terrorism" and cooperate on immigration.

A draft declaration prepared for the 27 ministers from Europe and around the Mediterranean -- from Algeria through the Middle East to Syria and Turkey -- said they resolved to strengthen their partnership to enhance stability and reinforce democratic institutions ..."including the rule of law, democracy and human rights".
The draft, for a communique to emerge from the two-day conference, has already seen several changes.

Before the meeting, human rights groups including Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, and Reporters Sans Frontieres, called on the ministers to take further action to safeguard rights and press freedom.
Under the draft, the ministers would ..."intensify work on human rights whilst respecting ... value systems through an increased number of activities.

"They underline the importance of maintaining and developing the direct involvement of civil societies, among others via networking between non-governmental organisations legally established in their country of origin."

They would also ..."establish active cooperation in the field of combating terrorism, which constitutes a flagrant violation of human rights...(and) wage a determined campaign against racism and xenophobia and intolerance..."

Human Rights Watch said that the situation in many parts of the region remained grave ..."with consequences ranging from the disruption of the Oslo process in the Israeli-Palestinian arena to the enormous loss of life in Algeria...
"In many European countries a mood of hostility towards immigrants, sometimes erupting in violence, continues to grow."

It said that while Barcelona 1995 had given a blueprint recognising the central place of human rights in constructing a region of stability and prosperity, their protection over the past year meant ..."the process appears to be at the crossroads."

It said decisions at the Malta conference -- a followup to Barcelona -- would be crucial in setting the course for the next year ... "when the Palestinian-Israeli negotiations and efforts to resolve Algeria's civil war may reach their decisive stages."

Reporters Sans Frontieres asked the EU to intervene to save press freedom. It named Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco and the occupied territories as countries that violated that freedom, with Algeria, the Palestinian Autonomous Territories, Syria, Turkey and Tunisia doing so "on a massive scale".
